content: {"id": "d4f25fcc-8780-48d8-9a0f-543e9034c297", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "A Windows Server 2016 EC2 instance with a third-party antivirus installed returns 0 applicable updates on every scan and occasionally fails installs with 0x80070005 access denied on WinSxS files. Why is Microsoft not offering any updates and how do I unblock it?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "05f11575-056a-40ca-9ff6-8f4b7b59414a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Windows Server 2016 Updates Not Available Access Denied"}]}

{"id": "ee3112eb-ab5a-4262-9939-9df37c08ba56", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This is a known pattern on Windows Server with third-party AV, and it's almost always one (or a combination) of these causes rather than an EC2/AWS-specific issue:

## Why 0 applicable updates shows up

**1. AV is interfering with the Windows Update client itself**
Many third-party AV products hook into or filter file system I/O (especially on WinSxS, SoftwareDistribution, and the Windows Update stack's DLLs/services). If the AV is quarantining, blocking, or locking files that `wuauserv`/`TrustedInstaller` need to read during the applicability scan, the scan can silently come back empty instead of erroring. "0 applicable" is what you get when the detection logic can't actually evaluate the catalog against your installed component store — not necessarily that nothing is missing.

**2. Corrupted or inconsistent WinSxS / component store**
The 0x80070005 (ACCESS_DENIED) on WinSxS files during install is a strong signal the component store itself is in a bad state — either because AV is holding handles/locks on those files during servicing operations, or because permissions/ACLs on WinSxS got altered (sometimes AV real-time protection rewrites ACLs when it quarantines/restores a file). TrustedInstaller needs exclusive, unimpeded access to WinSxS during servicing; any AV filter driver intercepting that can produce exactly this error.

**3. Windows Update Agent reading a stale/corrupt scan cache**
If prior scans failed due to AV interference, the SoftwareDistribution store can get into a bad state and keep reporting 0 applicable updates until it's reset.

## How to unblock it

1. **Add AV exclusions for the Windows Update / servicing paths** (this is the most common fix):
   - `C:\Windows\WinSxS\*`
   - `C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution\*`
   - `C:\Windows\servicing\*`
   - `C:\Windows\System32\catroot2\*`
   - Processes: `TrustedInstaller.exe`, `TiWorker.exe`, `svchost.exe` (for wuauserv), `dism.exe`, `wusa.exe`
   
2. **Check for AV-driven ACL/permission changes on WinSxS**: run `icacls C:\Windows\WinSxS` and compare against a known-good instance of the same AMI/build. If ACLs were modified, you may need to re-run `icacls` to restore inheritance (`icacls C:\Windows\WinSxS /reset /T /C` — test carefully, this is sensitive) or restore from a snapshot.

3. **Reset the Windows Update components** after exclusions are in place:
   ```
   net stop wuauserv
   net stop cryptSvc
   net stop bits
   net stop msiserver
   ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
   ren C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 catroot2.old
   net start wuauserv
   net start cryptSvc
   net start bits
   net start msiserver
   ```
   Then re-run the scan.

4. **Run the DISM health check** to confirm the component store integrity once AV is out of the way:
   ```
   DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth
   DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth
   ```
   If corruption is found, `/RestoreHealth` (needs network access to Windows Update or a local source).

5. **Temporarily disable real-time AV protection** and re-run the update scan as a diagnostic — if updates suddenly show up as applicable, that confirms the AV is the blocker, and you can scope exclusions precisely rather than guessing.

6. If this is fleet-wide, check whether the AV vendor has a published Windows Update compatibility/exclusion list for Server 2016 — most enterprise AV vendors (CrowdStrike, Trend Micro, Sophos, McAfee, etc.) publish specific exclusion guidance for WSUS/WU compatibility.

Want me to check this specific instance's current state — e.g. pull WindowsUpdate logs via Systems Manager, check the instance's patch baseline/compliance status in SSM, or look at whether other instances in the same fleet are hitting the same 0x80070005?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
